title: I have no internet
summary: Separates Wi-Fi, cable, DNS and router causes, and tells you which to fix first without wasting time on the wrong one.

scope.question: What exactly is failing?
scope.help: Distinguishing 'no network' from 'connected but no web pages' points you at completely different parts of the system.

options.label: No network icon, or it says no internet access
Connected to Wi-Fi or a cable, but web pages will not load
Only some sites or apps will not work

wifi_or_cable.question: Are you using Wi-Fi or an Ethernet cable?
wifi_or_cable.help: The two have almost no shared failure modes, so identifying which you use saves a lot of time.

options.label: Wi-Fi
Ethernet cable
Both are available and both fail

wifi_strong.question: Does the Wi-Fi show a strong signal with a password, and does another device on the same network have internet?
wifi_strong.help: If other devices work, the router and internet connection are fine and the fault is on this PC.

options.label: Strong signal, connected, but other devices work fine
Weak signal, or keeps disconnecting
No Wi-Fi adapter appears at all

wifi_driver_state.question: Do other devices on the same Wi-Fi network have internet right now?
wifi_driver_state.help: This is the key test. Working other devices mean the router and ISP are fine.

options.label: Yes, other devices work
No, nothing in the house works

wifi_range.question: Does the signal improve if you move closer to the router?
wifi_range.help: Weak signal is usually a placement, interference or adapter problem rather than an internet problem.

options.label: Yes, it improves when I move closer
No, the signal is weak right next to the router

wifi_missing_adapter.question: Does the Wi-Fi adapter appear in Device Manager at all?
wifi_missing_adapter.help: Check Device Manager > Network adapters. A missing adapter usually means a driver or hardware switch problem, not a network problem.

options.label: It shows a yellow exclamation mark or an error code
It is not listed at all
I have not checked yet

cable_link_lights.question: Do the lights on the Ethernet port and on the router's matching port light up when the cable is connected?
cable_link_lights.help: No link lights means no physical connection, which is a cable, port or driver problem rather than an ISP problem.

options.label: Yes, both ends have lights
No, no lights on one or both ends

other_device_cable.question: Does another device connected by the same cable and port get internet?
other_device_cable.help: If another device works with the same cable, the cable and port are fine and the fault is in this PC's network stack.

options.label: Yes, another device works
No, it fails too

dns_check.question: Can you open a website by its web address, such as https://1.1.1.1, even though names like example.com fail?
dns_check.help: If a numeric address works but names do not, DNS resolution is the problem. Opening a numeric address means bypassing name lookups entirely.

options.label: Yes, numeric addresses work but names do not
No, nothing loads
I have not tested that

partial_access.question: Is the problem specific to work or school sites that require sign-in, or to one particular app?
partial_access.help: Some networks require a sign-in page before any other traffic is allowed, which looks exactly like a broken connection.

options.label: Only sites that require a login fail
One specific site or app fails
Everything is slow rather than broken

result_tcp_ip_reset.title: Reset the TCP/IP stack on this PC
result_tcp_ip_reset.diagnosis: Other devices work, so the router and your internet connection are fine. The fault is in this PC's network configuration.
steps: Open Command Prompt as Administrator: right-click Start > Terminal (Admin), or search cmd and choose Run as administrator
Run ipconfig /flushdns to clear the cached name lookups
Run ipconfig /release and then ipconfig /renew to get a fresh address from the router
Run netsh winsock reset to rebuild the Winsock catalog
Run netsh int ip reset to rebuild the TCP/IP stack
Restart the PC, then test again. If it still fails, download our network reset script and run it instead of typing commands by hand
warnings: Netsh resets can temporarily disrupt VPN or virtual machine software. Uninstall or reinstall those afterwards.
Only run these as Administrator from Command Prompt, not PowerShell.

result_dns_fix.title: Change your DNS servers
result_dns_fix.diagnosis: Numeric addresses working while names fail means your DNS resolver is the problem, not your connection.
steps: Open Settings > Network & internet > Wi-Fi or Ethernet, then the Properties button for your connection
Under DNS server assignment choose Edit, then switch it to Manual
Enter 1.1.1.1 and 1.0.0.1 as preferred and alternate DNS, or 8.8.8.8 and 8.8.4.4 for Google's
Save, then run ipconfig /flushdns in an elevated Command Prompt
Test with our DNS lookup tool on this site to confirm resolution is working
Turn the Wi-Fi adapter off and on after changing DNS so it applies immediately
warnings: Some workplace and school networks supply their own DNS and block others, so ask your administrator before changing it there.

result_dns_flush.title: Clear the DNS cache first
result_dns_flush.diagnosis: Flushing the cache is harmless, takes seconds, and fixes a surprising share of name-resolution problems.
steps: Open an elevated Command Prompt
Run ipconfig /flushdns
Then run ipconfig /release followed by ipconfig /renew
Restart the browser, which keeps its own DNS and connection state
If the problem persists, change your DNS servers to 1.1.1.1 as described in the DNS guide
Use our DNS lookup tool to check whether your chosen resolver answers correctly

result_signal_strength.title: Improve the Wi-Fi signal
result_signal_strength.diagnosis: Weak signal slows everything and causes dropouts even when the connection technically works.
steps: Move the router to a higher, open position rather than inside a cupboard or behind a TV
Move away from microwaves, cordless phone bases, baby monitors and Bluetooth speakers
Check how many walls are between the PC and router, and consider a mesh node or a wired connection instead
On a desktop, use Ethernet instead of Wi-Fi where practical, since it is both faster and more reliable
Check the router's 5 GHz and 2.4 GHz bands, since 2.4 GHz travels further but 5 GHz is faster where the signal is strong
Update the Wi-Fi adapter driver, since some older drivers handle weak signals poorly
warnings: Avoid long cable runs through doorways or under carpets with Ethernet. PoE or a powerline adapter is better in that situation.

result_wifi_driver.title: Clean reinstall the Wi-Fi driver
result_wifi_driver.diagnosis: A corrupt or outdated Wi-Fi driver causes everything from no connection to random dropouts.
steps: Open Device Manager and expand Network adapters
Right-click the Wi-Fi adapter and choose Uninstall device, ticking Delete the driver software
Restart the PC and let Windows install a basic driver automatically
Then install the official driver from your PC vendor, or from the adapter manufacturer
Update the chipset driver as well, since the Wi-Fi driver depends on it
If the adapter disappears after restarting, check the physical Wi-Fi switch or function key and the BIOS setting for wireless
warnings: Removing the driver leaves you without Wi-Fi. Have Ethernet or a USB Wi-Fi dongle available in case the automatic install fails.
On a laptop, the Wi-Fi card may be disabled by a function key or a BIOS switch rather than a driver problem.

result_device_manager_code.title: Read the Device Manager error code
result_device_manager_code.diagnosis: Device Manager tells you exactly what the driver complaint is, and each code has a specific fix.
steps: Open Device Manager with the Windows key plus X, then Device Manager
Expand Network adapters and double-click the adapter with the yellow exclamation mark
Read the code on the General tab, which will be something like Code 10, 28, 43 or 31
Look that code up in our Device Manager error guide for the specific fix
Code 28 means no driver at all, so install from your PC vendor; Code 10 and 43 are usually fixed by a clean reinstall
Run Scan for hardware changes from the Action menu if you have added hardware recently
warnings: Do not delete driver files from C:\Windows\System32 by hand. Use the Device Manager uninstall button with the delete option instead.

result_hardware_switch.title: Check for a hardware switch or BIOS setting
result_hardware_switch.diagnosis: A missing adapter on a laptop is usually a switch, a key combination or a BIOS setting rather than a dead adapter.
steps: On a laptop, check for a physical Wi-Fi switch on the side and a function key combination such as Fn plus F2 or F12
Press the combination and recheck Device Manager
Enter the BIOS with the Del or F2 key at power-on and look for Wireless or WLAN in the security or advanced settings
If the adapter is listed in Device Manager but greyed out, right-click it and choose Enable device
Check hidden devices using View > Show hidden devices for a disabled adapter
If BIOS has no wireless option at all, the adapter is not being detected, which points to hardware failure
warnings: Do not keep a wireless card disabled to avoid interference, since it will also affect Bluetooth and Wake on LAN.

result_cable_or_port.title: Fix the physical Ethernet connection
result_cable_or_port.diagnosis: No link lights means the connection is not established physically, so software fixes will not help.
steps: Reseat both ends of the cable firmly, listening for a click
Try a different port on the router and a different port on the PC, since ports do fail
Test with a different known-good Ethernet cable, as damaged cables are extremely common
Check for damage, sharp bends or crushed cable near the connectors
On a laptop, check the Ethernet adapter is enabled and has a current driver in Device Manager
Update the LAN driver from your PC vendor if link lights appear but no internet follows

result_captive_portal.title: Complete the network sign-in page
result_captive_portal.diagnosis: Public and guest networks require a sign-in page to be opened and accepted before any other traffic is allowed.
steps: Open a browser and navigate to http://neverssl.com, which forces a sign-in page to appear if one is required
If nothing appears, try http://1.1.1.1
Accept the terms, or sign in with whatever credentials the network requires
For phone hotspots, some Android versions keep a sign-in page in a separate browser window, so check for other browser windows
Some corporate networks need a certificate installed, which requires your IT administrator
If you cannot get the sign-in page at all, restart the connection and try again from a fresh network
warnings: Never disable certificate warnings or antivirus to force a sign-in page through. That is how captive portal credential theft works.

result_single_service.title: Work out whether it is DNS or the service itself
result_single_service.diagnosis: When only one site fails, the network is probably fine and the problem is name resolution or the service.
steps: Use this site's DNS lookup tool to see whether the failing domain resolves
If it resolves, the problem is the service or your path to it rather than DNS
Try the service in a different browser or in a private window to rule out extensions
Check whether the site works on another device on the same network
Flush the DNS cache with ipconfig /flushdns and try once more
If a proxy or VPN is enabled, turn it off and test again
warnings: If you use a corporate proxy, ask your administrator which proxy addresses are allowed before changing any settings.

result_router_or_isp.title: The problem is the router or the ISP
result_router_or_isp.diagnosis: When nothing in the house works, the fault is the router, the modem or your internet provider, not any single PC.
steps: Reboot the modem first, wait a full 60 seconds, then reboot the router and wait another 60 seconds
Check whether the router's status lights show a normal internet or WAN connection
Connect a device directly to the modem with an Ethernet cable to bypass the router
Note the modem's and router's indicator lights, then call your provider and read them out
Check whether your provider has a service outage in your area
If the modem's internet light stays off even after a reboot, the modem or the provider's line is at fault
warnings: Do not reset the modem to factory settings before calling your provider, since that often erases the credentials they need for your line.
Avoid interrupting a firmware update if the modem lights are flashing in a pattern, since that can brick it.
